In [[mathematics]], a function ''f'' of ''n'' variables ''x''<sub>1</sub>, ..., ''x''<sub>''n''</sub> leads to a '''Chisini mean''' ''M'' if, for every vector ⟨''x''<sub>1</sub>, ..., ''x''<sub>''n''</sub>⟩, there exists a unique ''M'' such that{{r|graziani}} 
:''f''(''M'',''M'', ..., ''M'') = ''f''(''x''<sub>1</sub>,''x''<sub>2</sub>, ..., ''x''<sub>''n''</sub>).

The [[arithmetic mean|arithmetic]], [[harmonic mean|harmonic]], [[geometric mean|geometric]], [[generalised mean|generalised]], [[Heronian mean|Heronian]] and [[quadratic mean|quadratic]] means are all Chisini means, as are their weighted variants.

While [[Oscar Chisini]] was arguably the first to deal with "substitution means" in some depth in 1929,{{r|graziani}} the idea of defining a mean as above is quite old, appearing (for example) in early works of [[Augustus De Morgan]].<ref>De&nbsp;Morgan, Augustus.  "Mean" in [https://babel.hathitrust.org/cgi/pt?id=njp.32101074718923&view=1up&seq=41 ''Penny Cyclopaedia''] (1839).</ref>{{or?|date=May 2023}}
